subject: Request: Temporary quota uplift for Nimbus product launch (SLA/latency considerations)
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch week: short-term quota uplift request / latency SLA questions

Hi Ben,

Quick note — Nimbus is going live with a phased national rollout on 2026-09-21 for our new scheduling feature. We expect a concentrated spike in inference traffic during the first 48–72 hours (attached forecast).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift to our token quota and burst window to cover ~25M additional tokens over the 72-hour launch window?
- We need confirmation that the latency SLA (p95) for our tier will be maintained during the uplift, and what fallback behavior (throttling/fairness) would apply if capacity is constrained.

We have a procurement kickoff next week; procurement@ has the contract questions but asked that technical feasibility be confirmed first.

Attachment: nimbus-prod-launch-traffic-forecast.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Thanks — appreciate a quick read and a yes/no so we can plan procurement.

— Samantha
Director, Product Ops
Nimbus Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week: short-term quota uplift request / latency SLA questions

Samantha — thanks for the details and the forecast. Quick summary from my side:
- We can support a temporary uplift but need to formalize the window, exact token bump, and any contractual amendment for SLAs/credits.
- During elevated usage, requests are still subject to our fairness policies; we can provide a higher priority carveout for the launch that reduces the chance of throttling, but absolute p95 latency guarantees require a Dedicated or reserved capacity add-on.

Two asks for you:
1) Can you confirm the exact start/end times for the 72-hour window (timezone) and final token totals?
2) If procurement can sign a short amendment for a time-bound uplift and a one-time usage payment, legal can approve faster.

Looping in my internal ops: I will send a note to Marissa (sales leadership) and Vivek (capacity) to propose a temporary uplift and the operational controls (canary throttles, auto-rollback).

Attachment referenced: SLA-exception-request-form.pdf

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nimbus launch — temporary quota uplift & SLA/latency follow-up

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Nimbus' request. Key points:
- Request: +25M tokens over a 72-hour window starting 2026-09-21 (Samantha attached forecast).
- Customer asks that p95 latency remain within their current SLA tier; they understand Dedicated gives stronger guarantees but are asking for a time-bound priority adjustment.

Proposed operational controls:
- Time-bound elevated quota applied to their API key for the exact 72-hour window (UTC times to be confirmed).
- Canary policy: route 10% of traffic to elevated path for first 30 minutes, monitor p95 and error rates.
- Auto-rollback: if p95 > 2x baseline or error rate increases >0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes, rollback uplift and notify customer.
- Billing: one-time usage invoice for overage; legal to sign SLA amendment for the uplift window and carveout language.

Risk notes: if we accept without capacity reservation, other customers may see transient performance impact. We can reduce risk by applying a temporary priority class that still respects fairness but limits cross-customer interference.

Requesting:
- Marissa: commercial OK on short-term billing amendment and credit policy?
- Vivek: capacity/ops OK on canary + rollback and ability to provision the elevated priority for 72 hours?

Original message below.

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nimbus launch — temporary quota uplift & SLA/latency follow-up

Ben / Vivek — I reviewed the forecast and the deal. Commercially we can do a time-bound uplift with these conditions: 
- Customer signs the attached one-page amendment (SLA-exception-request-form.pdf) covering the exact uplift window, billing terms, and rollback triggers.
- We include a hard cap on absolute tokens consumed during the window (we should set this at forecast + 10% margin) to protect platform fairness.
- No SLA credit will apply if uplift is accepted without Dedicated reservation; we will offer an alternate pricing credit if we fail to meet agreed rollback triggers due to Redwood-side issues.

Vivek — please confirm ops can set priority class and implement the canary/rollback policy by 2026-09-20 EOD. If there are capacity risks, flag them here so I can surface to leadership and propose a short burst reserve.

Once we have ops confirmation, Ben — please send the amendment to procurement and ask them to sign so legal can fast-track.

— Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary uplift approved (next steps & DocuSign)

Samantha — good news: we have commercial approval with conditions. Summary and next steps:
- Approved uplift: +25,000,000 tokens for a 72-hour window. Provisional window proposed: 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-24T00:00:00Z (please confirm if that aligns with your rollout).
- Operational controls: 10% canary for first 30 minutes; auto-rollback triggers (p95 > 2x baseline OR error rate > 0.5% for 5 min). We will cap consumption at forecast +10%.
- Billing: one-time invoice for the uplift (terms in amendment). No standard SLA credit will be provided for uplift windows unless we fail rollback guarantees under Redwood control — in which case we will provide the agreed commercial credit.

Actions:
1) Samantha/procurement: sign the one-page amendment here: https://www.docusign.com/record/ABC-7890-NBH (DocuSign).
2) Samantha: confirm the exact UTC start/end times (if different) and confirm the forecast totals so we can set the hard cap.
3) Vivek/ops: provision priority class and schedule monitoring runbook for 09/21 UTC.

Attachment: SLA-exception-request-form.pdf (requires signature)

If procurement wants a faster path we can accept a signed PO + email attestation while DocuSign completes, but legal prefers the amendment to be signed pre-launch.

Thanks — we'll standby for confirmation and will run the canary the moment you flip the switch.

— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-exception-request-form.pdf
